summary: A value, or a low–high range, picked along a track. For a rough value in a known range, where where-it-sits matters more than the exact number.
useWhen: the value is a position in a known range and roughly right is right — a threshold, a zoom, a volume
a filter bounds a quantity from both ends — "between 30s and 2m", "$20 to $80" — pass `[low, high]`
seeing the value's place in the range helps the choice more than typing it would

useInstead.when: the exact number matters — a price, a budget, a count someone will be held to
useInstead.why: dragging to exactly 4,250 is a test of hand steadiness; a field takes the number as typed

useInstead.when: there are a few named choices, not a continuum — Low, Medium, High
useInstead.why: a slider with three stops hides the names behind positions and reads out numbers nobody chose

useInstead.when: the value is on or off
showing how far something has got, not asking for a value
useInstead.why: a track with a knob invites a drag; progress is not something the user sets

requires: `label` or `aria-label` — the group's name, and every thumb's name through it
`formatOptions` whenever the number has a unit — the formatted value is what is read out, so a percentage without it is announced as "0.7"
guarantees: every thumb is a visually hidden `<input type="range">`: arrows step, Page Up and Down jump a tenth of the range, Home and End go to the bounds
`aria-valuetext` carries the formatted value — "70%", "120 sec" — in the user's locale
a range's thumbs are named with the label — "Minimum Duration" and "Maximum Duration" — and cannot cross; each stops at the other's value
pressing the track moves the nearest thumb there
every thumb's target is 24px square, around a 20px knob, and the track is 24px tall — WCAG 2.5.8
thumbs at the bounds stay inside the component; the track is inset by half a thumb
in a right-to-left locale the track runs right to left, and the arrow keys follow it
a disabled slider's thumbs are disabled inputs, out of the tab order
`description` is linked to every thumb with `aria-describedby`
a range with `name={[low, high]}` submits two form fields
notes: the value beside the label is an `<output>` with `aria-live="off"`: the thumb already announces each change, and a second voice would read every step twice
`onChange` fires on every step of a drag; `onChangeEnd` fires once when it ends. Fetch, filter a server or save on `onChangeEnd`
`thumbLabels` names a range's two thumbs and defaults to English "Minimum" and "Maximum" — pass translations

antiPatterns.why: an exact number across millions is out of reach by drag — each pixel is thousands
`onChange` fires on every pixel of a drag — dozens of requests for one gesture, answered out of order

antiPatterns.do: <Slider label="Threshold" minValue={0} maxValue={1} step={0.01} formatOptions={{ style: 'percent' }} />
antiPatterns.why: without a format the value is shown and read as "0.7"; with it, "70%"

antiPatterns.dont: two Sliders for the low and high end of one filter
antiPatterns.why: two separate sliders can cross — a minimum above the maximum — and read as two unrelated settings

antiPatterns.dont: a Slider with three steps standing in for Low, Medium, High
antiPatterns.why: the choices have names; a slider reads them out as 1, 2 and 3
